II_arunachal-pradesh.title: Arunachal Pradesh — Incredible India (Ministry of Tourism)

RG_ETIQ.title: Culture and etiquette in India — Rough Guides

ARF_FOOD.claim: Rice, fish, meat and vegetables, gently flavoured, often with bamboo shoots; try momos, thukpa and boiled rice cakes.

evidence.quote: The heart of its cuisine include rice, fish, meats, and an abundance of vegetables.
Here, flavours emerge gently, harnessing the essence of herbs, organic produce, and the unique addition of bamboo shoots.
You must taste Momos and Thukpa during your visit and the Boiled rice cakes are a delightful snack, savoured throughout Arunachal Pradesh, offering a taste of tradition.
The official language of the state is Meitei (also known as Manipuri).

MNF_AREA.claim: About 22,327 sq km, mostly hills around the Imphal Valley.

evidence.quote: The total area covered by the state is 22,327 km2 (8,621 sq mi).

MNF_AIR.claim: Bir Tikendrajit International Airport, Imphal, has direct flights to Kolkata, Guwahati, Delhi, Bengaluru and Agartala.

evidence.quote: Bir Tikendrajit International Airport is situated in the capital Imphal which connects direct flights from Imphal to Kolkata, Guwahati, New Delhi, Bangalore and Agartala.

MNF_CAP.claim: Imphal is the capital and gateway.

evidence.quote: The capital city of Manipur, Imphal , serves as the gateway to this enchanting state.

MNF_RAIN.claim: Rain falls between April and mid-October; summer highs reach 32 °C and winters can be cool.

evidence.quote: The state receives an average annual rainfall of 1,467.5 mm (57.78 in) between April and mid-October.
The maximum temperature in the summer months is 32 °C (90 °F).
This northeastern corner of India enjoys a generally amiable climate, though the winters can be cool.

MNF_SANGAI.claim: The Sangai Festival, in November, showcases dance, music and traditional sports.

evidence.quote: The Sangai Festival, held in November, showcases the state's rich cultural heritage through dance, music, and traditional sports.

MNF_NINGOL.claim: Ningol Chakouba (around 9 November) is when married women return to their parents' home for a feast.

evidence.quote: Held on 9 November, this is a social festival of the Meitei people of Manipur where married women (Ningol) are invited (Chakouba, literally calling to a meal; for dinner or lunch) to a feast at their parental house accompanied by their children.

MNF_OTHER.claim: Other festivals include Yaoshang, Cheiraoba, Kang and the Shirui Lily festival.

evidence.quote: The festivals of Manipur are Lui-ngai-ni Ningol Chakouba, Shirui Lily festival, Yaoshang, Gan-ngai, Chumpha, Cheiraoba, Kang and Heikru Hidongba, as well as the broader religious festivals Eid-Ul-Fitr, Eid-Ul-Adha and Christmas.

MNF_SHOES.claim: Remove your shoes before entering a temple or mosque; socks are fine.

evidence.quote: When entering a temple or mosque , remove your shoes and leave them at the door (socks are acceptable and protect your feet from burning-hot stone ground).

MNF_HAND.claim: Eat, pass and accept things with your right hand.

evidence.quote: Rule one is: eat with your right hand only .
In general, you should accept things given to you with your right hand – though using both hands is a sign of respect.

MNF_DRESS.claim: Dress modestly, with legs and shoulders covered.

evidence.quote: Women are expected to dress modestly, with legs and shoulders covered.

MNF_PHOTO.claim: Don't photograph images of deities or inside temples unless you are sure it is allowed.

evidence.quote: Hindus are very superstitious about taking photographs of images of deities and inside temples; if in doubt, desist.

MLF_LANG.claim: English, Khasi and Garo are official languages.

evidence.quote: English, Khasi, and Garo are the official languages of Meghalaya.
Meghalaya covers an area of approximately 22,429 square kilometres

MLF_AIR.claim: Shillong's airport is at Umroi, 30 km away on the Guwahati–Shillong highway.

evidence.quote: State capital Shillong has an airport at Umroi 30 kilometres (19 mi) from Shillong on the Guwahati-Shillong highway.

MLF_RAIN.claim: Some areas get up to 12,000 mm of rain a year — the wettest place on Earth.

evidence.quote: With the average annual rainfall as high as 12,000 mm (470 in) in some areas, Meghalaya is the wettest place on Earth.

MLF_TEMP.claim: It rarely passes 28 °C; sub-zero winter nights are common.

evidence.quote: The maximum temperature in this region rarely goes beyond 28 °C (82 °F), whereas sub-zero winter temperatures are common.

MZF_CAP.claim: Aizawl is the capital and has the state's airport.

evidence.quote: Mizoram's airport is at the capital city of Aizawl.
Mizo and English are the official languages of the state.
Mizoram covers 21,081 square kilometres (8,139 sq mi), of which 84.53% is forested, making it the 4th-most forested state in India.
Mizoram has a humid, subtropical climate with temperate to warm summers ranging from 20 to 30 °C (68 to 86 °F).
Winters experience a cool and arid ambiance in a temperature range of 10 to 20 °C (50 to 68 °F).
The region is influenced by monsoons, raining heavily from June to September which sustains high humidity and lush forestry.

MZF_CHAP.claim: Chapchar Kut, the spring festival, falls in February–March.

evidence.quote: The Chapchar Kut, celebrated in February-March, marks the onset of spring with colorful dance performances and traditional rituals.

NLF_CAP.claim: Kohima is the capital; Chümoukedima–Dimapur is the largest city.

evidence.quote: Its capital city is Kohima and its largest city is the twin Chümoukedima–Dimapur.
The majority of the population in the state speaks English, which is the official language of the state.
The state has an area of 16,579 square kilometres (6,401 sq mi)
Annual rainfall averages around 1,800–2,500 millimetres (70–100 in), concentrated in the months of May to September.

NLF_WIN.claim: Winters rarely drop below 4 °C, though frost is common up high.

evidence.quote: In winter, temperatures do not generally drop below 4 °C (39 °F), but frost is common at high elevations.

NLF_HORN.claim: The Hornbill Festival runs 1–10 December at Kisama Heritage Village, 12 km from Kohima.

evidence.quote: Hornbill Festival is an annual festival celebrated from 1 to 10 of December in the Northeastern Indian state of Nagaland.
Just 12 kms from Kohima, you can discover the Kisama Heritage Village, where the world-famous Hornbill Festival comes to life.

TRF_CAP.claim: Agartala is the capital and largest city.

evidence.quote: Tripura is divided into eight districts and 23 sub-divisions, where Agartala is the capital and the largest city in the state.

TRF_LANG.claim: Bengali, Kokborok and English are official.

evidence.quote: Bengali, Kokborok, and English are the state's official languages.
The third-smallest state in the country, it covers 10,491 km2 (4,051 sq mi)

TRF_AIR.claim: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, 12 km from Agartala.

evidence.quote: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, located 12 km northwest of Agartala at Singerbhil, is the second busiest airport in northeast India after Guwahati.

TRF_SEASONS.claim: Winter December–February, summer March–April, monsoon May–September, post-monsoon October–November.

evidence.quote: The four main seasons are winter, from December to February; pre-monsoon or summer, from March to April; monsoon, from May to September; and post-monsoon, from October to November.
During the monsoon season, the south west monsoon brings heavy rains, which cause frequent floods.

evidence.quote: Durga Puja, Kali Puja, Dolyatra, Ashokastami and the worship of the Chaturdasha deities are important festivals in the state.
Some festivals represent confluence of different regional traditions, such as Ganga puja, Garia puja, Kharchi puja and Ker puja.

places.name: Arunachal Pradesh
places.summary: India's largest monastery at Tawang, high passes, the Apatani valley of Ziro and wild forests — with an Inner Line Permit.
places.seoTitle: Arunachal Pradesh Travel Guide: Tawang, Ziro & Permits
places.seoDescription: Plan Arunachal Pradesh: the Inner Line Permit, Tawang Monastery, Sela Pass, Dirang, Bomdila, Ziro, Mechuka, Namdapha and getting there.

overview.text:
Arunachal Pradesh is the largest of the Northeast's seven sister states, with over 500 orchid species. Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit, available online as an e-ILP.

The classic route crosses Bomdila and Dirang and climbs over the 4,170 m Sela Pass to Tawang, home of India's largest Buddhist monastery. Elsewhere are the Apatani valley of Ziro, remote Mechuka and Namdapha's forests.

items.body: Momos and thukpa — the two dishes every visitor should taste, found right across the whole state.
Boiled rice cakes — a traditional snack eaten throughout Arunachal Pradesh.
Bamboo shoots — the distinctive ingredient that flavours many tribal dishes.
Everyday meals — rice with fish, meat and plenty of vegetables, gently flavoured with local herbs and organic produce.

overview.text:
Manipur is home to Loktak, the largest freshwater lake in Northeast India, famous for its floating phumdis — and to the Sangai deer, found only in Keibul Lamjao National Park.

It is considered the birthplace of modern polo and is famed for Manipuri classical dance. The Sangai Festival is held in November.

places.name: Meghalaya
places.summary: The 'abode of clouds': living root bridges, record rainfall at Sohra, waterfalls, caves and Khasi villages.
places.seoTitle: Meghalaya Travel Guide: Shillong, Cherrapunji & More
places.seoDescription: Plan Meghalaya: Shillong, Cherrapunji, the living root bridges, Nohkalikai Falls, Mawlynnong, Laitlum, getting there and the best time.

images.alt: Boats on the clear Umngot river at Dawki
images.caption: Umngot river, Dawki

overview.text:
Meghalaya's Khasi and Jaintia peoples belong to one of the world's largest surviving matrilineal cultures. Their living root bridges, grown from rubber fig roots, are on UNESCO's tentative list.

Shillong, the capital, is the base. To the south, Cherrapunji (Sohra) still holds the records for the most rain in a month and a year, with Nohkalikai, India's tallest plunge waterfall, the Mawsmai cave and the trek to Nongriat's double-decker root bridge.

overview.text:
Mizoram — the 'land of the hill people' — borders Myanmar and Bangladesh. It became a Union Territory in 1972. Mizo society runs on Tlawmngaihna, a code of hospitality and unselfishness.

Aizawl is the capital; Reiek, Dampa, Champhai and Murlen, the 230 m Vantawng Falls and Phawngpui, the highest peak, are the main draws.

overview.text:
Nagaland is known as the 'Land of Festivals', and its best-known — the Hornbill Festival — runs every year from 1 to 10 December at the Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima.

Dimapur is the gateway on the plains; Kohima, the capital, holds the Commonwealth War Cemetery from the 1944 battle; Mokokchung is the cultural heart of the Ao Naga. Khonoma, India's 'first green village', and the high Dzükou Valley are the classic outings from Kohima.

overview.text:
Tripura is home to 19 tribal communities, and its name is believed to come from the goddess Tripura Sundari, whose temple at Udaipur is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas.

Agartala, the old Manikya capital, has the Ujjayanta Palace; Neermahal is India's largest water palace; Unakoti's rock carvings are on UNESCO's tentative list.
